'''Pinikura''' (Pinigura, Binigura, Binnigoora) is an extinct [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] formerly spoken along the [[Ashburton River (Western Australia)|Ashburton River]] in the state of [[Western Australia]] by the [[Binigura]]. It is closely related to [[Thalanyji language|Thalanyji]],<ref>{{Citation |last=Austin |first=Peter |title=2. The classification of Pinikura, Western Australia |date=2008-06-12 |work=Current Issues in Linguistic Theory |volume=298 |pages=31–41 |editor-last=Bowern |editor-first=Claire |url=https://benjamins.com/catalog/cilt.298.05aus |access-date=2026-03-12 |place=Amsterdam |publisher=John Benjamins Publishing Company |language=en |doi=10.1075/cilt.298.05aus |isbn=978-90-272-4814-5 |editor2-last=Evans |editor2-first=Bethwyn |editor3-last=Miceli |editor3-first=Luisa}}</ref> which all Binigura now speak.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Austin |first=Peter |date=30 June 1988 |title=Aboriginal languages of the Gascoyne-Ashburton region |url=https://opal.latrobe.edu.au/articles/journal_contribution/Aboriginal_languages_of_the_Cascoyne-Ashburton_region/22201855 |journal=Working Papers in Linguistics |pages= |doi=10.26181/22201855}}</ref> Ten speakers of Pinikura were recorded in 1975, but none since then.<ref name=AIATSIS />
